l1.title: Example: Google Docs meeting notes from a template
l1.summary: Create a document, name it, insert the built-in meeting notes template and replace each placeholder with the real date, attendees, agenda and action items.
key_points: Name the document in the title box at the top left, then press Enter
A new empty page offers template chips; Insert, then Building blocks, has the same templates
Replace every placeholder before you finish
Keep action items as a bulleted list with an owner and a date
Docs saves by itself: wait for the saved indicator

recovery: If no template chip is shown, open Insert, then Building blocks, then Meeting notes.
If the page is not empty, move the cursor to a new line before inserting the template.
l2.detail:
1. Open a new blank document.
2. Click the title box at the top left, type the meeting name and press Enter.
3. On the empty first line choose the Meeting notes chip, or use Insert, Building blocks, Meeting notes.
4. Replace the date, attendees, agenda and action item placeholders.
5. Wait until Docs reports the document as saved.

Notes: Observed on 2026-10-30: a new empty document showed template chips, among them Meeting notes and Email draft. Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Google Docs weekly status report with headings and bullets
l1.summary: Write a short status report with a title and three headed sections (done, next, blockers) with bullet lists. Pick headings from the styles menu and check the outline panel.
key_points: Choose headings from the styles menu; that works in every account
If Markdown shortcuts are on, # and - may convert by themselves: look at the result before retyping
The outline panel lists the headings that took effect
Use one bullet per item and keep each item to one line
Wait for the saved indicator before leaving

recovery: If a heading did not apply, select the line and pick the style from the styles menu.
If a list started by itself, undo once and retype the line as plain text.
l2.detail:
1. Open a new document and name it in the title box.
2. Type the first section name on its own line and apply Heading 2 from the styles menu.
3. Press Enter, start a bullet list and add one item per line.
4. Repeat for the next sections.
5. Check the outline panel shows every heading, then wait for the saved indicator.

Notes: Observed on 2026-10-30 in one account: a line starting with # became Heading 1 and a line starting with - started a list, so check the result instead of assuming either behavior. Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Google Docs one-page brief with a table
l1.summary: Name the document, add headed sections, then insert a table from the Insert menu and fill it cell by cell with Tab.
key_points: Insert, then Table, opens a size grid: hover to the size you want, then click
Tab moves to the next cell; Tab in the last cell adds a row, so skip it there
Type the header row first, then the data rows
Check that the table fits the page width before moving on
Wait for the saved indicator

recovery: If an extra empty row appears, delete that row from the table menu.
l2.detail:
1. Open a new document and name it.
2. Write the section headings and short paragraphs.
3. Put the cursor on an empty line, open Insert, choose Table and click the grid cell for the size you need.
4. Type the header cells, pressing Tab between cells, then the data rows.
5. Stop pressing Tab after the last cell.
6. Wait for the saved indicator.

Notes: Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Google Sheets daily work log
l1.summary: Keep a header row (date, task, hours, status), add one row per task and total the hours with a formula in a separate cell.
key_points: Click a cell to select it, then just type; Tab moves right and Enter usually goes back to the start of the next row
A formula starts with an equals sign; without it the text stays plain
Type dates as year-month-day to avoid day and month swaps
A new sheet can show a dialog over the grid: press Escape or choose OK before typing
Wait for the saved indicator before leaving

recovery: If typing does nothing, click a cell first so the grid has focus.
If a promo or table dialog covers the grid, press Escape or choose OK, then click a cell again.
l2.detail:
1. Open a new spreadsheet and dismiss any dialog over the grid.
2. Click the first cell and type the header: Date, Task, Hours, Status, using Tab between cells.
3. Press Enter to move to the next row and add one row per task.
4. In a cell below the Hours column type an equals sign, SUM and the Hours range to total the hours.
5. Wait for the saved indicator.

Notes: Observed on 2026-10-30: a new spreadsheet opened with a Save time with tables dialog and a promo banner, and the grid did not accept typing until a cell was selected. Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Google Sheets expense tracker with totals
l1.summary: Create columns for date, item, category and amount, add the rows, then add a total cell with a sum formula and format the amount column as currency.
key_points: Put the header in row 1 and type amounts as plain numbers, without a currency symbol
Total with an equals-sign formula, for example a sum over the amount column
Format the amount column as currency from the Format menu
Freeze the header row from the View menu if the list will grow
Wait for the saved indicator

recovery: If a number is shown as text, retype it without symbols or spaces.
l2.detail:
1. Open a new spreadsheet.
2. Type the header: Date, Item, Category, Amount.
3. Add one row per expense, typing the amount as a plain number.
4. Under the Amount column add a total with an equals sign and SUM over the amounts.
5. Select the Amount column and apply the currency format from the Format menu.
6. Wait for the saved indicator.

Notes: Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Gmail compose an email and send it only after confirmation
l1.summary: Open Compose, add the recipients, subject and body of the email, review it and press Send only after the user has confirmed the recipients and the text. Drafts save by themselves.
key_points: A recipient becomes a chip after Enter, comma or Tab
Fill the subject before the body and type above any signature
Gmail saves a draft automatically; closing the window keeps it in Drafts
Sending cannot be taken back after the short undo window: confirm recipients and text first
Attach files with the paperclip button and wait until the upload finishes

recovery: After Send, the Undo link stays for a few seconds; use it at once if a mistake is spotted.
If the draft is not wanted, discard it from the trash icon in the compose window.
l2.detail:
1. Click Compose.
2. Type each recipient and press Enter so it becomes a chip.
3. Type the subject, then click the body and write the message above any signature.
4. Take a snapshot and read the recipients, subject and body back to the user.
5. Press Send only after the user confirmed.

Notes: Gmail keeps unsent work in Drafts. Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Google Calendar create an event with guests
l1.summary: Create an event with a title, date and time, optional guests and a description. Saving with guests can ask whether to send invitations, so confirm that choice with the user.
key_points: Use Create, then Event, or click a free time slot
Set the date and time fields before adding guests
A guest becomes a chip after Enter
Saving with guests asks about invitation emails: choose deliberately
Check the time zone shown under the time fields

recovery: If the event landed on the wrong day, drag it or edit the date field and save again.
l2.detail:
1. Click Create, then Event.
2. Type the title.
3. Set the date and the start and end time.
4. Add guests one at a time, pressing Enter after each.
5. Click Save; if Calendar asks whether to send invitations, ask the user first.
6. Confirm the event appears on the right day.

Notes: Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Google Slides add an image and keep it inside the slide
l1.summary: Open or add a slide, insert an image from the Insert menu, resize it from a corner handle and check that it stays within the slide before leaving.
key_points: Insert, then Image, offers several sources such as upload or Drive
Resize from a corner handle to keep the aspect ratio
Check that nothing spills past the slide edge in the normal view
Slides saves by itself: wait for the saved indicator

recovery: If the image spills past the slide, drag a corner handle inward until it fits.
l2.detail:
1. Open the presentation and select the slide.
2. Open Insert, choose Image and pick the source.
3. When the image appears, drag a corner handle to resize it.
4. Look at the slide: the whole image must stay inside the edge.
5. Wait for the saved indicator.

Notes: Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Google Forms build a short feedback form
l1.summary: Name the form, add a few questions with the right types, mark the important ones required and preview it. Do not share it with anyone until the user asks.
key_points: Rename the untitled form at the top before adding questions
Add a question with the plus button in the side toolbar
Pick the question type from the dropdown on the question card
Use the required switch for must-answer questions
Use Preview to check the form; sharing is a separate step

recovery: If a question has the wrong type, change it from the dropdown on the same card.
l2.detail:
1. Open a new blank form and type its name.
2. Type the first question and choose its type, for example multiple choice or paragraph.
3. Add the remaining questions with the plus button.
4. Switch Required on for the important ones.
5. Open Preview to check the result and leave sharing for the user.

Notes: Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Notion create a page from a template
l1.summary: Create a new page, choose a template from the template list, give the page a title and fill in the template's properties and sections.
key_points: Start from New page; the template list is shown on an empty page
Type the title in the first line before editing the body
Use the slash menu inside the page to add blocks such as headings and to-do items
Fill the page properties, for example date and status, at the top
Notion saves by itself; wait for the sync indicator

recovery: If the template did not apply, open the page menu and choose the template again.
l2.detail:
1. Click New page.
2. On the empty page choose a template from the list.
3. Type the page title in the first line.
4. Fill the properties at the top and the sections below, using the slash menu for new blocks.
5. Wait for the sync indicator.

Notes: Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Medium save a clean draft without publishing
l1.summary: Click the title and the body separately, type with one Enter between paragraphs, check that the draft shows as saved and leave it unpublished.
key_points: Click the title area and type the title, then click the body and type the story
Use one Enter between paragraphs: two leave an empty paragraph
Check the saved status text
Reopen the draft to confirm the content persisted
Do not press Publish unless the user asked

recovery: If an empty paragraph appears, remove it with Backspace and check the saved status again.
l2.detail:
1. Open a new story.
2. Click the title area and type the title.
3. Click the body separately and type the paragraphs with one Enter between them.
4. Wait for the saved status.
5. Reopen the draft and check the title and paragraphs are still there.

Notes: Based on a 2026-10-16 observation in a signed-in editor: two line breaks created an unwanted empty paragraph. Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Google Drive find a file and open it
l1.summary: Use the search box at the top, type part of the file name, press Enter and open the result. Check the owner and modified date when several files share a name.
key_points: Search matches names and content; add a file type filter to narrow the results
A single click selects a file and a double click opens it
Check the owner and last modified columns when names repeat
Look in Shared with me and Recent for files you did not create
Do not delete or move files unless asked

recovery: If nothing matches, try fewer words or remove the file type filter.
l2.detail:
1. Open Drive.
2. Click the search box and type part of the file name.
3. Press Enter.
4. Read the result list: name, owner, last modified.
5. Open the right file with a double click.
6. Never delete or move anything unless the user asked.

Notes: Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Wikipedia collect a few facts for a note
l1.summary: Search for the topic, open the article, read the lead paragraph and the infobox, and note two or three facts with the section they came from. Follow the citations for anything important.
key_points: The lead paragraph and the infobox hold the most reliable summary facts
A disambiguation page lists several topics: pick the right one
Use the citation numbers to find the source of a claim
Note the page title and the date you read it
Look for a banner that warns about disputed or unsourced content

recovery: If the article is a disambiguation page, open the entry that matches the topic and read that article instead.
l2.detail:
1. Search for the topic and open the article.
2. Read the lead paragraph.
3. Read the infobox on the right.
4. Write down two or three facts with the section name.
5. Open the citation for any claim that matters and note its source.

Notes: Example written for testing recall on 2026-10-30; check each step against the live page.

l1.title: Example: Google Docs project proposal from the template gallery
l1.summary: Create a new document from a built-in project proposal, meeting notes, resume or letter template, preserving its layout while replacing the sample content.
key_points: Open Docs home, then Template gallery; choose the template by purpose, not a fixed screen position
Choosing a gallery template creates a new document; confirm its URL before editing
Rename the top-left title with native keyboard input and Enter; a DOM value alone may not save
Keep the template layout and replace sample text; leave labeled blanks only for a reusable blank form
Wait for saved-to-Drive, then reopen the document to check the title and layout

recovery: Template names and categories vary with account language; inspect the gallery labels.
If renaming reverts, click the title box and use actual keyboard input followed by Enter; verify after reopening.
If the editor is canvas-based, inspect its rendered page; a toolbar-only snapshot does not prove body content.
l2.detail:
1. Open the Google Docs home page and choose Template gallery (템플릿 갤러리 in the observed Korean UI).
2. Select a template for the requested purpose. A project proposal template was observed creating a new editable document.
3. Click the top-left document title, select its text and type a meaningful name through native keyboard input, then press Enter.
4. Replace the template's sample text using the user's supplied details. Preserve the existing headings, tables and layout. Do not invent missing names, dates or amounts; use labeled blanks when the user wants a reusable template.
5. Wait for the saved-to-Drive status, reopen the newly created document and inspect its content and layout.

Notes: Gallery creation was observed in the real Google Docs Korean UI through Arise on 2026-11-01. This is a built-in example, not a Gatekeeper-reviewed contribution or a speed benchmark. Template availability and labels can vary.

l1.title: Example: Google Docs purchase request form with an item table and approval fields
l1.summary: Create a reusable purchase, leave or expense request document with labeled fields, a real table and a review or approval section.
key_points: Create a new document and name it through native title-box typing, then Enter
Click the visible document page before typing; the hidden accessibility textbox is not a usable click target
Add a title, requester fields, a reason and an approval area; use labeled blanks for a reusable template
Insert a real table with Insert, Table; Tab between cells and stop in the last cell
Apply heading styles, wait for saved-to-Drive, then reopen the document to check its layout

recovery: If the snapshot's document textbox is offscreen, click the visible page in a fresh screenshot and type through the native keyboard.
If a table has an extra last row, remove only that empty row; Tab from the last cell adds a row.
If a heading or list converted automatically, inspect the result before adding another style; Markdown shortcuts depend on Docs preferences.
l2.detail:
1. Open a new blank Google Docs document. Rename it in the top-left title box with actual keyboard input and press Enter.
2. Click the visible document page. For a purchase request template, add a title, document number, request date, requester/department, purchase reason and a review/approval area. Use labeled blanks when creating a reusable blank form; use only supplied values when filling one.
3. Apply a heading using the Styles menu. On the observed macOS setup, Command+Option+1 applied Heading 1 to the title.
4. Position the caret on the items line. Open Insert (삽입), then Table (표), and use the size grid. The live example used four columns and three rows: Item, Quantity, Unit price, Amount, followed by two blank item rows.
5. Type into each table cell and press Tab only between cells. Do not press Tab after the final cell.
6. Wait for the saved-to-Drive indicator. Reopen the document and inspect the title, fields and table; check that the table remains within the document width. Creating the form does not submit it for approval.

Notes: A purchase request template with a Heading 1 title, requester fields, reason, approval area and a four-column/three-row table was created using native Arise input in real Google Docs on 2026-11-01. This built-in example is not a reviewed catalog publication or a speed benchmark.

l1.title: Example: Google Flow create a short video from a text prompt
l1.summary: Choose a video mode and model available to the account, enter the user's prompt, check the displayed credit cost, then wait for a finished clip and preview it.
key_points: Use the video creation mode currently available in this project and account
Check the selected model and its displayed credit cost before each generation
A Pending card or spinner is still in progress; wait for an explicit completed clip
Preview the result and check the requested subject, motion and framing
Keep the output private; sharing or publishing requires the user's direction

recovery: If the requested mode or model is unavailable, stop before generating and report the account limitation.
If Flow stays Pending or reports an error, inspect its notification and credit state before retrying; do not submit a duplicate.
l2.detail:
1. Open Google Flow in a desktop Chromium browser and start or open the user's intended project.
2. Choose the text-to-video creation mode and an available model.
3. Enter only the user's requested prompt. Check the selected model and displayed credit cost before submitting.
4. Generate one clip, wait for a completed result, then preview it and check the requested subject and motion.
5. Leave the result private unless the user asks to share, publish, or export it.

Notes: Built-in example drafted from Google Flow's public product and help pages on 2026-11-01. The authenticated creation UI was not available for observation in this session; exact controls, model availability and credit costs can vary. This example is not verified site knowledge and is not benchmark evidence.

l1.title: Example: Google Flow turn reference frames into a video
l1.summary: When Frames to Video is available, select authorized starting and ending frames, check their order and the model cost, then generate and inspect the resulting motion.
key_points: Confirm the Frames to Video mode is available in the current account before preparing the task
Use only reference images supplied by the user or otherwise authorized for this task
Check frame order, selected model and displayed credit cost before generation
Wait for a completed clip, then preview whether it follows the intended frames
Pending or error states are not successful output; avoid blind retries

recovery: If Frames to Video is not available, do not substitute another mode without the user's direction.
If the clip is Pending or failed, inspect status and credit information before any retry.
l2.detail:
1. Open the intended Google Flow project and confirm that Frames to Video is available in the current account.
2. Select only user-supplied or otherwise authorized starting and ending frames, and verify their order.
3. Add concise motion guidance, then check the selected model and displayed credit cost.
4. Generate one clip, wait for completion, and preview whether its beginning and ending follow the selected frames.

Notes: The public Google Flow product page lists Frames to Video as a capability, but the authenticated interface was not available for observation in this session. Treat these steps as a documentation-based example, check the current UI and cost, and do not treat this as a benchmark result.
